instruction: Get the image from the given link, crop it to a 500x500 pixel square with GIMP, and store it as 'cropped.jpeg' on your Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey("ctrl", "alt", "t"); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires cropping the downloaded image to a square of 500x500 pixels using GIMP. Custom getter extracts image dimensions, custom metric verifies they match 500x500. Similar complexity to original (download, open GIMP, perform operation, save file).

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the core requirement: image dimensions of 500x500 pixels
Getter logic is correct: retrieves file from VM, uses PIL to extract dimensions, returns width/height dict
Metric logic is correct: performs exact integer comparison of width and height against expected values
Data flow is sound: getter extracts image dimensions -> metric compares dimensions -> expected values (500x500) match instruction requirement
Expected values are semantically correct: 500x500 matches the instruction's cropping requirement
Implementation handles edge cases: checks for None results, missing dimension values, and logs errors appropriately
Practical feasibility confirmed: PIL can extract dimensions from JPEG files, metric can compare integers
